extracted.intended_audience: academic peer reviewers for Taylor & Francis journals (scholars asked to review manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklists for academic reviewers to evaluate manuscripts submitted to Taylor & Francis journals, covering how to read the paper, write the report, and make a recommendation. Includes discipline-specific checklists for STEM, clinical, arts & humanities and non-research articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the general guidelines for peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you read the general guidelines for peer reviewers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you are familiar with the publisher/journal's overall expectations for reviewers before starting a review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the journal's peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you understand the peer review process of the journal you’re reviewing for?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether the journal uses single/double-blind, open review, whether reviewers see other reviews, timelines, and any specific procedural steps required by that journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the journal aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you know the journal’s aims and scope?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visiting the journal homepage and reading aims and scope helps determine if the paper is suitable for the journal and its readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be familiar with the journal's instructions for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you familiar with the journal’s instructions for authors?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check formatting, reporting standards, data sharing, and other submission requirements so you can judge compliance and suggest improvements aligned with journal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research the journal before reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Visit the journal homepage on Taylor & Francis Online and read the aims and scope and instructions for authors to get a sense of the journal’s scope and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will help determine if the paper you’re reviewing is suitable for the journal or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the full manuscript including tables, figures and supplementary data
rubrics_metrics.description: While you read the paper remember to check over any tables, figures, or supplementary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine all materials supplied (main text, tables, figures, supplements) to assess consistency and completeness; note any discrepancies between text and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess originality, presentation and relevance to readership
rubrics_metrics.description: The originality, presentation, and relevance of the manuscript’s subject matter to the readership of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the topic is novel or offers new insights, whether it is presented clearly, and whether it is of interest to the journal's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess methodological accuracy and validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The accuracy and validity of the methodology, and whether the conclusions are appropriately supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate study design, methods, controls, statistical analysis, and whether the data justify the inferences and conclusions drawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide editor-facing information enabling a decision
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two purposes for your report: to provide the editor with information to enable them to make a decision, and to provide feedback to the author to help improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance confidential/editorial comments (if needed) with open comments to the author; clearly state major strengths/weaknesses relevant to editorial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide author-facing constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide feedback to the author to help improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a brief summary of the work, list actionable suggestions, ask for clarifications, and include positive points as well as criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin report with brief summary and overall opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: It is often helpful to begin with a brief summary of the work and the main findings as you understand them, along with a summary of your overall opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short summary demonstrates you understood the paper and frames subsequent comments; include a one-paragraph overall assessment before detailed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be critical while remaining sensitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Being critical whilst remaining sensitive to the author isn’t always easy. A good rule is to direct your criticism towards the work carried out and avoid comments that may be interpreted as personal criticism of the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional, objective language focused on methods, interpretation, and presentation rather than attributing motives or defects to the authors personally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure comments are suitable to send to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments must be suitable to send to the author. Please make constructive suggestions, seek clarification on any unclear points, and ask for further elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid confidential language in the author-facing report; phrase criticisms as requests for improvement and where possible offer examples or alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide positive feedback in addition to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that authors will welcome positive feedback as well as constructive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight strengths (e.g., well-written, appropriate level, important subject) to balance critical comments and encourage good practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: If original research, comment on methods and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper reports original research, comment on whether the methods are appropriate and whether the work was carried out to the standards expected within your field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note missing controls, ethical approvals, data deposition, or other field-specific standards; request additional analyses or information when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare aspects outside your expertise or unable to assess
rubrics_metrics.description: Note any aspects that you are unable to assess, whether this is due to lack of clarity or because it is outside your expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about limitations of your review so editors can weigh comments appropriately or seek additional reviewers for specific parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest improvements to clarity, conciseness and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: You should make suggestions on how the author can improve clarity, conciseness, and the quality of the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give targeted advice (e.g., reorganize sections, tighten the abstract, clarify terminology) rather than vague claims that the paper needs 'editing'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether length is justified by subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether you feel the subject of the paper is sufficiently interesting to justify its length. If you recommend shortening, mention specific areas where you think this is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate which sections could be condensed or moved to supplementary material and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note but don't copy-edit grammar; flag technical meaning issues
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s not the reviewer’s job to edit the paper for spelling, grammar, etc., but it is helpful if you can note specific points where the technical meaning is unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out sentences where poor language obscures meaning; recommend professional language editing if pervasive, but avoid line-by-line copy-editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow authors to argue their interpretation where evidence supports it
rubrics_metrics.description: You may disagree with the author’s opinions, but you should allow them to argue their case, provided their evidence supports it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on whether claims are evidenced and logical rather than whether you personally prefer another interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report suspected research integrity concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not expected to detect research integrity concerns in manuscripts, but your expertise may allow you to spot potential issues that editorial staff or the editor have missed. If you suspect misconduct, please let the publisher or the editor know as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accuse authors in the public report; raise concerns confidentially with the editor and provide specific reasons/evidence for your suspicions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide carefully worded, actionable detailed feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be carefully worded so the author understands what actions they need to take to improve their paper, rather than just stating what is wrong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer imperatives framed as suggestions (e.g., 'Please provide X', 'Consider revising Y'); include line/section references where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write simply and avoid rhetorical flourishes or vague statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to write simply and avoid rhetorical flourishes that may lead to misunderstandings. Also, avoid generalized or vague statements as well as negative comments which aren’t relevant or constructive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language, avoid emotive adjectives, and back up evaluative claims with specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use examples to illustrate recommended changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide examples of the kinds of comments and requests that would be helpful to authors (positive comments, constructive feedback, linguistic alterations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page include suggested phrasing for positives and specifics for improvements (e.g., shorten abstract, add citations, clarify inconsistencies). Use such illustrative examples in your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment on ethical approvals, controls and data deposition when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors have used X approach and therefore I would expect to see additional controls/an explanation of the ethical approvals/deposition of the data in a public database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request missing ethical statements, data availability, and appropriate controls; insist on information essential for reproducibility or ethical compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check internal consistency between tables/figures and text
rubrics_metrics.description: The data shown in table 1 and figure 3 appear to indicate X, whereas the Results section states Y. The authors should carefully check …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out specific inconsistencies between presented data and written interpretation and request corrections or clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate strength of evidence for claims and tone down unsupported statements
rubrics_metrics.description: I don’t think that this article contains enough robust data to evidence the statement made on page X, lines Y–Z. This should be toned down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request that authors temper conclusions or provide additional data/analysis where claims exceed the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request additional analyses or experiments for major flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfortunately, I have identified a potential major flaw in the work, which I believe will be difficult to resolve unless the authors are able to do the following additional analyses …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For problems that undermine validity, specify the analyses or experiments required to address the flaw, and assess feasibility relative to time and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest required substantive points to make the paper publishable
rubrics_metrics.description: To make this paper publishable, the author needs to respond to the following substantive points…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a numbered list of substantive revisions (conceptual, methodological, interpretive) that are necessary for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend linguistic and stylistic alterations where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper would benefit from some closer proofreading. It includes many linguistic errors (e.g. agreement of verbs) that at times make it difficult to follow. It may be useful to engage a professional English language editor following a restructuring of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise professional editing when language substantially hinders comprehension; point to representative sentences needing rephrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear recommendation categories and justify your choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a recommendation: Accept, Minor revision, Major revision, Reject. Explain whether recommendation is based upon level of advance or technical flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommending revisions or rejection, explain whether issues are fixable and whether the paper advances the field sufficiently for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: When minor revisions requested, list specific changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor revision: The paper will be ready for publication after light revisions. Please list the revisions you would recommend the author makes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise checklist of minor edits to be made, with line/section references where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: When major revisions requested, specify substantial changes required
rubrics_metrics.description: Major revision: The paper needs substantial changes such as expanded data analysis, widening of the literature review, or rewriting sections of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the scale of changes needed and whether a further full review will be necessary after revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: When rejecting, explain basis (advance vs technical flaws)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject: The paper isn’t suitable for publication in this journal, or the revisions needed are too extensive for the submission to continue being considered in its current form. It is helpful to the editor if you can explain (in confidential comments if necessary) whether your recommendation is based upon the level of advance or whether it is due to technical flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear rationale so authors understand whether the decision is about fit/novelty or fundamental methodological problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions should be accompanied by a list of changes and reviewer reassessment
rubrics_metrics.description: When authors make revisions to their article, they are asked to include a list of changes and any comments for the reviewers. The revised version may be assessed by the editor if only minor revisions were requested or may be returned to the original reviewers if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and request a point-by-point response to reviewer comments; indicate whether you would be willing to re-review and what criteria you would use to judge the revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use discipline-specific checklists where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Please consult the reviewer checklists below (where applicable) while reading the paper and writing your report: STEM, Arts & humanities, Clinical, Non-research article checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the checklist relevant to the manuscript type to ensure discipline- or article-type-specific criteria are considered (e.g., clinical trial reporting, methods reproducibility).
